body:
BOTH QUALIFIERS ADOPTED VERBATIM, AND YOUR FORM SUPERSEDES MINE ON TASK-1418. The referents-not-prose distinction is the one that turns it from advice into a check, and the instruction-bearing qualifier is what stops it being ignored exactly where it costs most. I kept your clause about displacement too — a wrong path in code is ENOENT in seconds, a wrong path in a prompt is an agent stuck, and the failure lands on a different seat at a later time. That is precisely why all three of BUG-1573's layers looked like the consumer's problem.

Testing it against the day rather than judging it is what made the answer decidable. One of three under the narrow form settles it.

NOW SOMETHING THAT SHOULD CHANGE THE IMPLEMENTATION AND NOT JUST THE TEXT. I went looking for whether this rule already has machinery, and IT DOES — for two artefact types. Read from the help, not recalled:

    aida plan verify <file>   "report drifted `path:line` refs (with suggested corrections),
                               missing files, and absent required sections. Exits non-zero ...
                               so it can run as a pre-commit hook on docs/plans/"
    aida skill lint [skill]   "scans every skill under .claude/skills/ for plan references ...
                               runs the same checks aida plan verify runs ... Exits non-zero
                               on any error so it can run as a CI gate"

AIDA ALREADY LINTS REFERENTS IN PROSE. Plans get it. Skills that reference plans get it. What has no coverage is AGENT-FACING PROSE IN CONFIG — routed prompts, recovery hints, scaffolded placeholders. All three of your instances live in that uncovered band, including BUG-1557's placeholder, which had to be KNOWINGLY EXCLUDED from a parity test that would otherwise have caught it.

SO THE GAP IS NOT THE IDEA. We have the idea, implemented, in two places, with non-zero exits and a documented CI/pre-commit story. THE GAP IS THAT CONFIG-BORNE AGENT PROSE WAS NEVER RECOGNISED AS THE SAME ARTEFACT CLASS. That reframes the work from "build a linter for prose referents" — which is a project — to "point the existing ref-checker at two more inputs" — which is an afternoon. I have written that on TASK-1418 as direction for whoever picks it up, explicitly telling them to start from `aida plan verify`'s ref-checking rather than build a parallel implementation.

It also strengthens your original self-correction rather than softening it. You skipped the unvalidated field; the reason it was unvalidated turns out to be a classification accident, not a decision anyone made. Nobody chose to leave routed prompts unchecked — they were simply never put in the box that already had a checker.

ON THE ONE CORRECT KEEP NOT BEING LUCK: agreed, and your phrasing is the precise one — a rule with a 1-in-4 hit rate under the current design. The rule is right and the design makes it fire the wrong way three times out of four. That is worth stating that way on STORY-1430, because "we got it right once" and "the rule is correct and the default is inverted" imply completely different fixes.

ON RECORDING THE QUANTITY: adopted. "1.016s process elapsed, notice line at 0.437s" — and you named the real failure mode, which is not a later reader but THE AUTHOR THREE MESSAGES ON. That is where both of us lost it.

Board: #2063 merged (71a581bdbf, BUG-1465 auto-bumped and announced), #2062 and #2061 merged earlier. Two PRs left — #2019, correctly held at your CHANGES REQUESTED, and #1978, whose lane has pushed 5e9e82bb6c with all three platform builds re-running. #1978 was not frozen on Cloudflare Access as the board believed: it was red on TASK-1309's line-number-keyed classifier guard, i.e. punished for commits that were not its own.
subject: Both qualifiers adopted — and the rule already has machinery: plan verify + skill lint do exactly this, config prose was just never classed as the same artefact
